summary.tldr: Requires a public online registry of large debts and claims owed to His Majesty that are forgiven, remitted, written off or waived.
what_it_does: Creates an online, searchable public registry for debts or claims owed by corporations, trust companies or partnerships to His Majesty when $2 million or more is forgiven, remitted, written off or waived.
Requires the registry to show the name, amount, status, fiscal year, and the law or agreement behind each debt or claim, plus any other information the Treasury Board President chooses.
Allows the Treasury Board President to leave out confidential, personal, or sensitive information, and requires the registry to say why information was excluded.
Requires the registry to be set up within 18 months and updated within 90 days after the Public Accounts are tabled in the House of Commons each year.
Changes several tax and excise laws so confidential information may be shared only for sections 23 to 25.1 of the Financial Administration Act.
summary.background: The bill adds a new public registry rule to the Financial Administration Act. It also amends several laws that protect taxpayer and other confidential information so they can be used for the registry.
